events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text:
Hi Erkki, I'm at the site now. Changed the SFP on transmission node TRN-042.
Link is up and alarms cleared, but traffic is still not coming back. Have you seen this before?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Yes. Is this one of the older units?

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Yes, installed around 2019 I think.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Ok. Don't trust the green link status on those.
Sometimes after changing the SFP the interface comes up normally, but the forwarding state doesn't recover correctly.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: So another SFP?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
No. Usually the SFP is fine.
Check whether the traffic counters are actually increasing. If they stay at zero even though the interface is UP, it's probably the issue I've seen before.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Yes. Link UP. RX power looks normal. Counters basically zero.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
That's it.
Disable the interface, wait a little, then enable it again. Don't reboot the whole unit unless that fails.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Did that. Traffic is back 👍

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text: Good. These old units sometimes behave like this after an optical module replacement.

events.author: Veikko Vikkelä
events.text: Is this documented somewhere?

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Not that I know of 😄
We've just learned it over the years.

events.author: Erkki Expert
events.text:
Subject: RE: TRN-042 traffic not recovering after SFP replacement

Hi Veikko,

That sounds like the behaviour we have seen with some of the older transmission units.

The confusing part is that everything can look normal after replacing the optical module:

- interface status = UP
- optical levels = OK
- alarms = cleared

...but traffic still doesn't recover.

Before replacing the SFP again or rebooting the unit, check the traffic counters.

If the interface is UP but the counters remain at zero, try disabling and enabling the interface once.

This has solved the issue in several cases I've seen.

I don't think this is written in the normal field instructions. It is one of those things we have learned from experience.

Regards,
Erkki
